frequency_question: How often does an emerging market central bank deploy an incremental or special reserve ratio tool within a given multi-year period?
membership_rule: Includes any formal announcement by a major emerging market central bank of a temporary, incremental, or marginal reserve ratio or cash reserve ratio requirement aimed at managing systemic liquidity surpluses. Excludes permanent baseline statutory reserve ratio adjustments.

cases.name: PBoC reserve requirement ratio targeted cut/adjustment cycles
Central Bank of Brazil compulsory deposit requirement adjustments
Bank of Russia temporary reserve requirement modifications

provenance_note: 5 cases named, 15 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (3.0x)
coverage_note: 5 named historical instances; believed roughly 15 comparable regulatory cycles globally over the window.
known_gaps: Does not account for idiosyncratic domestic banking sector liquidity distributions or specific policy frameworks of individual countries.
skeleton: Major emerging market central banks facing liquidity overhangs, evaluated across 5-year observation blocks since 2010, yielding a baseline historical recurrence frequency.
multiplier: 5 representative jurisdictions x 3 observation blocks = 15 comparable institutional instances, with 4 recorded occurrences of ad-hoc incremental reserve ratio deployments.
validity_reason: Central bank liquidity management frameworks evolve slowly over multi-year regulatory regimes, keeping base rates stable for several years.
